plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (MgF2/Al2O3 defect cavity filter) based on iteration_05 results. Three complementary routes implement the feedback directives: bilateral symmetry constraints, bounded thickness search around round-2 medians, and L-BFGS-B solver. Route variations test material sensitivity and layer count effects while preserving the core defect-cavity scientific principle.

routes.title: Symmetry-constrained MgF2/Al2O3 defect cavity with L-BFGS-B bounded optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Imposing bilateral symmetry constraints on mirror layer pairs and restricting thickness search to ±5 nm around round-2 medians will reduce the optimization degrees of freedom sufficiently for L-BFGS-B to converge to a locally optimal phase-matched configuration, improving target score without increasing layer count.
routes.design_principle: Defect-cavity bandpass filter with symmetric Bragg mirrors. Symmetry reduces search space dimensionality while preserving the resonant transmission mechanism at 255–280 nm.
routes.proposed_topology: 17-layer stack: Air | [MgF2/Al2O3]_8 mirror | MgF2 defect cavity | [Al2O3/MgF2]_8 mirror | fused silica substrate. Explicit layer sequence: L1(MgF2), L2(Al2O3), L3(MgF2), L4(Al2O3), L5(MgF2), L6(Al2O3), L7(MgF2), L8(Al2O3), L9(MgF2), L10(Al2O3-defect), L11(MgF2), L12(Al2O3), L13(MgF2), L14(Al2O3), L15(MgF2), L16(Al2O3), L17(MgF2).
design_variables: layer thicknesses with bilateral symmetry constraints: L13=L16, L6=L15, L7=L14; thickness bounds ±5 nm around round-2 medians
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
expected_advantages: symmetry ensures phase matching between mirrors
bounded search prevents unphysical thickness excursions
known_risks: symmetry constraint may prevent discovery of superior asymmetric solutions
±5 nm bounds may be too restrictive if round-2 medians are suboptimal
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 17-layer MgF2/Al2O3 defect-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate. Layer sequence: L1(MgF2), L2(Al2O3), L3(MgF2), L4(Al2O3), L5(MgF2), L6(Al2O3), L7(MgF2), L8(Al2O3), L9(MgF2), L10(Al2O3-defect), L11(MgF2), L12(Al2O3), L13(MgF2), L14(Al2O3), L15(MgF2), L16(Al2O3), L17(MgF2). Impose bilateral symmetry: thickness(L13)=thickness(L16), thickness(L6)=thickness(L15), thickness(L7)=thickness(L14). Initialize thicknesses at round-2 medians: defect L10=85.5 nm, inner mirrors L1-L6=44.0 nm, outer mirrors L11-L16=47.0 nm. Apply ±5 nm bounds around these medians. Use L-BFGS-B optimizer with max function evaluations=500, tolerance=1e-5. Spectral targets: maximize transmittance 255–280 nm, minimize transmittance 300–700 nm and 700–1100 nm. Air incidence, unpolarized. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directives: bilateral symmetry constraints on layers 13-16, 6-15, 7-14; ±5 nm thickness bounds around round-2 medians; L-BFGS-B solver with 500 max eval and 1e-5 tolerance.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 defect cavity with symmetry constraints to test material sensitivity
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing MgF2/Al2O3 with HfO2/SiO2 while maintaining the same 17-layer defect-cavity topology and symmetry constraints will yield comparable or improved target scores due to higher refractive index contrast, provided UV absorption in HfO2 remains low at 255–280 nm.
routes.design_principle: Same defect-cavity bandpass architecture as route_01, but with HfO2 (high-index) and SiO2 (low-index) material pair. Higher index contrast should widen the stopband and improve visible/NIR rejection.
routes.proposed_topology: 17-layer stack: Air | [SiO2/HfO2]_8 mirror | SiO2 defect cavity | [HfO2/SiO2]_8 mirror | fused silica substrate. Explicit layer sequence: L1(SiO2), L2(HfO2), L3(SiO2), L4(HfO2), L5(SiO2), L6(HfO2), L7(SiO2), L8(HfO2), L9(SiO2), L10(HfO2-defect), L11(SiO2), L12(HfO2), L13(SiO2), L14(HfO2), L15(SiO2), L16(HfO2), L17(SiO2).
design_variables: layer thicknesses with bilateral symmetry constraints: L13=L16, L6=L15, L7=L14; thickness bounds ±5 nm around scaled quarter-wave values at 267 nm center wavelength
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 requires ion-assisted deposition for density and UV transparency
SiO2/HfO2 pair is space-qualified for UV applications
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
higher index contrast yields wider stopband
expected_advantages: HfO2/SiO2 index contrast (~2.0/1.5) exceeds MgF2/Al2O3 (~1.38/1.65), potentially improving stopband rejection
HfO2 is moisture-stable with ion-assisted deposition
same symmetry constraints enable direct comparison with MgF2/Al2O3 route
known_risks: HfO2 may exhibit higher absorption at 255–280 nm than MgF2, reducing passband transmittance
HfO2 deposition requires ion-assistance for optimal UV performance

routes.title: 21-layer MgF2/Al2O3 defect cavity with extended mirror periods
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing mirror periods from 8 to 10 pairs per side (21 total layers) while maintaining symmetry constraints will improve visible/NIR stopband rejection depth without significantly degrading UV passband transmittance, as additional periods primarily affect stopband edges.
routes.design_principle: Extended defect-cavity architecture with more Bragg mirror periods. Additional layers increase stopband reflectivity at the cost of total thickness, but symmetry preserves resonant transmission mechanism.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:199509322 supports periodic SiO2/SiNx photonic crystal UV filter architecture with defect cavity, motivating the 17-layer and 21-layer topologies.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:211025653 documents HfO2/SiO2 as UV-transparent material pair with ion-assisted deposition stability, motivating route_01_refine_hfo2_sio2.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:16516444 supports ALD/IAD deposition methods for UV coatings, informing manufacturing considerations across all routes.
Prior iteration results (best_target_score 0.355) indicate room for improvement, motivating symmetry constraints and bounded search to refine convergence.
unresolved_decisions: Whether HfO2 absorption at 255–280 nm will significantly degrade passband transmittance compared to MgF2.
